key_insight: A Bayesian finite element model reconstructs steady blood-flow velocity and pressure from sparse noisy measurements while explicitly quantifying uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: This enables clinically useful flow-field estimation and derived metrics like pressure drop, flow rate, and wall shear stress without requiring offline training data.
method: Represent velocity and pressure with Taylor-Hood finite elements.
Use maximum-entropy physics-informed priors plus a noise likelihood to form a posterior.
Compute MAP via sparse nonlinear least squares; eliminate pressure analytically and use Laplace approximation for uncertainty.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on patient-specific cerebral aneurysm, aortic aneurysm, and aortic coarctation geometries, with reconstructions more accurate than tricubic interpolation and comparable to a PINN, and wall shear stress recovered more accurately than both.
watch_item: The approach targets steady 3D flows and depends on solver quality, mesh/basis choice, and the assumed noise model for reliable uncertainty estimates.
paper_title: Bayesian finite element regression for vascular flow reconstruction with quantified uncertainty
